title: Moral conviction and metacognitive ability shape multiple stages of information processing
description: Human electroencephalography (EEG) recordings from 80 participants who reported their attitudes on a set of sociopolitical issues and then viewed photographs of protests about those same issues. Each photo was preceded by a pie chart showing low, medium, or high social support for the issue. After each photo, participants rated their support for the protestors. The dataset supports investigation of how moral conviction and metacognitive ability shape multiple stages of information processing.
methods_description: Participants first provided attitudes on sociopolitical issues, then viewed protest photographs during EEG recording. Each photo was preceded by a pie chart indicating social support for the issue (low, medium, or high), and participants rated their support for the protestors after each photo.
